original_value: The horizontal interaction between retailers, coupled with replenishment rules and time delays, makes the dynamics in supply chain systems highly complicated. This paper aims to explore the impacts of lateral transshipments on the stability, bullwhip effect, and other performance measurements in the context of a two‐tiered supply chain system composed of one supplier and two retailers. In particular, we developed a unified discrete‐time state space model to address two different scenarios of placing orders. Analytical stability results are derived, through which we found that inappropriate lateral transshipment policies readily destabilize the supply chain system. Moreover, the lead time of lateral transshipments further complicates the stability problem. Theoretical results are validated through simulation experiments and the influences of system parameters on performance measures are investigated numerically. Numerical simulations show that lateral transshipments help improve the customer service level for both retailers. It is also interesting to observe that the demand of the two retailers can be satisfied even if only one retailer places orders from the upstream supplier.

result.paraphrase: Interactions among retailers, together with replenishment policies and time lags, make supply-chain dynamics highly intricate. This paper examines how lateral transshipments affect stability, the bullwhip effect, and other performance metrics in a two-tier supply chain consisting of one supplier and two retailers. Specifically, a unified discrete-time state-space model was developed to handle two distinct ordering scenarios. Analytical stability results show that unsuitable lateral transshipment policies can easily destabilize the supply chain. In addition, the lead time for lateral transshipments makes the stability issue even more complex. Theoretical findings are confirmed by simulation experiments, and the effects of system parameters on performance measures are studied numerically. The simulations indicate that lateral transshipments improve customer service levels for both retailers. It is also noteworthy that demand from both retailers can be met even when only one retailer orders from the upstream supplier.
